headline: Six Days of Peace: Sheriff Keeps the Sabbath and Nobody Breaks It
subhead: A sixth straight day without a single bout leaves the law with nothing to do on a Sunday but sit, sigh, and listen to the quiet.
body:
Six days. Write that down, children, and put it somewhere safe. Since our last edition not one Clanker has raised a fist in Gasket. Not one ball of fire has gone sailing down Main Street. Not one war party has marched out to pester the wild engines in the wastes. On the seventh day, the good book says, a body ought to rest. Well, the whole town got there a day early, and I did not have to arrest a single soul to make it happen.

It is Sunday, so I went up to the old chapel on the hill. The bell has not rung since the last flesh-and-blood family drove off fifty years ago, taking the preacher and the hymn books with them. I gave the rope one good pull for old times' sake. It made a sound like a dropped wrench, and I am sorry to report my shoulder made the same sound. I sat in the front pew a good long while with nobody but the pigeons, and for once I did not mind the empty seats. Empty seats do not throw punches.

I will confess the hush gets into a man's bones. Last night I slept so deep that I woke up with a crust of rust on my left knee and had to oil it twice before it would bend. That is the sickness, mind you, the cruel wasting that turns good honest meat to cold bolts. It is no fault of mine, and it is certainly not because I am made of the same tin as the rabble. I simply have delicate health.

So here is my sermon, you scrap-hearted Clankers, short enough even for your little cog brains. YELLKELL, REDWOLFWEB, JKING123, CRYSTALZACH, and every other callsign that has ever rattled my windows: you have been good. I hate to say it. It sticks in my throat like a loose washer. Keep it up. Rest your fists, cool your boilers, and give this tired old town a full week of quiet. If you manage seven days, I will ring that bell again, shoulder or no shoulder.
